```
Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about DuoAttention:

## Overview

DuoAttention is a framework that only applies a full KV cache to retrieval heads while using a light-weight, constant-length KV cache for streaming heads, which reduces both LLM's decoding and pre-filling memory and latency without compromising its long-context abilities.

## Key Concept

DuoAttention leverages the observation that only a fraction of attention heads, termed retrieval heads, are critical for processing long contexts, whereas streaming heads primarily focus on recent tokens. More specifically, only a fraction of attention heads, a.k.a, Retrieval Heads, are critical for processing long contexts and require full attention across all tokens. In contrast, all other heads, which primarily focus on recent tokens and attention sinks--referred to as Streaming Heads--do not require full attention.

## Head Identification Method

DuoAttention uses a lightweight, optimization-based algorithm with synthetic data to identify retrieval heads accurately.

## Performance Improvements

The method significantly reduces long-context inference memory by up to 2.55x for MHA and 1.67x for GQA models while speeding up decoding by up to 2.18x and 1.50x and accelerating pre-filling by up to 1.73x and 1.63x for MHA and GQA models, respectively, with minimal accuracy loss compared to full attention.

## Practical Capabilities

Combined with quantization, DuoAttention enables Llama-3-8B decoding with 3.3 million context length on a single A100 GPU.

## Code Availability

Code is provided in https://github.com/mit-han-lab/duo-attention.
```

```
Based on the web search results, here's what I found regarding MInference, Microsoft's sparse attention work, hybrid models, Mamba, and GLA:

## MInference: Microsoft's Sparse Attention Method

MInference leverages dynamic sparse attention to accelerate the pre-filling stage of long-context LLM inference, achieving up to 10x speedup for 1M contexts on a single A100. The method identifies three general patterns of sparse attention in long-context LLMs (A-shape pattern, Vertical-Slash pattern, and Block-Sparse pattern) and introduces a kernel-aware search method to assign the optimal attention pattern for each head.

## Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models

Recent works have proposed hybrid architectures that integrate state space models (SSMs) and attention components, which outperform non-hybrid models, especially in long-context language modeling compared to attention-only models and recall performance compared to pure SSMs.

Recent hybrid models vary along design axes including SSM layer type (Mamba is the most common), with a 1:1 SSM-to-attention ratio being typical, though some prefer more SSM layers for efficiency.

## GLA (Gated Linear Attention) in Hybrid Models

GLA (Gated Linear Attention) is a more expressive variant of linear attention with input-dependent gating that has been explored as a replacement for Mamba layers in hybrid architectures like Samba.

## Notable 2024-2025 Hybrid Models

Research has focused on LLMs consisting of a mixture of Mamba-2, self-attention, and MLP layers, with designs like an 8B-parameter Mamba-2-Hybrid containing 24 Mamba-2 layers, 4 self-attention layers, and 28 MLP layers.
```

```
I found comprehensive results about hybrid attention-SSM architectures, Mamba, Jamba, and sparse attention with NIAH benchmarking. Here's what the search revealed:

## Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Architectures

Jamba introduced the first large-scale hybrid Transformer–Mamba–MoE language model, with an architecture that interleaved attention and Mamba layers at a 1:7 ratio, with MoE layers added every two blocks. The architecture preserves linear prefill complexity while achieving up to 10× higher throughput and 2–3× lower latency than its predecessor.

## Design Variations

Research shows that a 1:1 SSM-to-attention ratio is typical, though some prefer more SSM layers for efficiency, and to retain efficiency many use sliding window attention (SWA) or combine SWA with full attention. Sequential fusion is the most common integration strategy, but parallel fusion is also explored.

## Sparse Attention and NIAH Benchmarking

Recent research systematically varies attention sparsification levels while monitoring retrieval performance, complemented by Just Read Twice (JRT) prompting to attempt recovery of SSM retrieval capabilities on NIAH for generation and prefill versions. Across model scales and architectural variants, as few as 15% of attention heads maintain near-perfect retrieval while complete ablation causes catastrophic failure, demonstrating that SSM layers do not contribute to retrieval.

## Recent Advances (2024-2025)

Mamba-3 is a new state space model designed with inference efficiency as the primary goal, with key upgrades including a more expressive recurrence formula, complex-valued state tracking, and a MIMO variant that boosts accuracy without slowing down decoding. Mamba-3 does not degrade retrieval capabilities on more real-world tasks like NIAH.
```

1	# TriangleMix Paper & 上游代码笔记
2	
3	> Paper: He et al., *TriangleMix: Accelerating Prefilling via Decoding-time Contribution Sparsity*, arXiv:2507.21526 v4。代码 <https://github.com/microsoft/MInference/tree/main/TriangleMix>。
4	
5	## 1. 算法本质
6	
7	**Triangle attention** 把 q 切两段，整体复杂度 O(N²) → O(N)：
8	
9	```
10	q1 = q[:, :, :-n_last]   # 前段：sink(n_init=8) + sliding window(n_local=512)，O(N · window)
11	q2 = q[:, :, -n_last:]   # 末段：跟全部 K dense attention，O(n_last · N) = O(N)，n_last=128
12	```
13	
14	`tri_mix.py:tri_shape_kernel`（30 行）：
15	
16	```python
17	def tri_shape_kernel(q, k, v, config):
18	    n_last = min(config["attn_forward_config"].get("n_last", 100), q.size(2) - 1)
19	    q1, q2 = q[:,:,:-n_last], q[:,:,-n_last:]
20	    y1 = a_shape_kernel(q1, k[:,:,:-n_last], v[:,:,:-n_last], config)  # sink + window
21	    qk = torch.einsum('bhmk, bhnk -> bhmn', q2, k) / math.sqrt(q.shape[-1])
22	    arange = torch.arange(n_last, device="cuda")
23	    mask = arange[None, None, :, None] >= arange[None, None, None, :]
24	    qk[:, :, :, -n_last:] = torch.where(mask, qk[:, :, :, -n_last:], -torch.inf)
25	    qk = torch.nn.functional.softmax(qk, dim=-1, dtype=torch.float32).to(q.dtype)
26	    y2 = torch.einsum('bhmn, bhnk -> bhmk', qk, v)
27	    return torch.cat([y1, y2], dim=2)
28	```
29	
30	**注意**：q2 看到的是**完整 K**（不是 K 末段），causal mask 仅作用在 q2 跟 K 末 n_last 之间。前面 K[:-n_last] 对 q2 全部可见。
31	
32	## 2. Layer dispatch（极简）
33	
34	`tri_mix.py:tri_mix_forward`（layer-level binary switch）：
35	
36	```python
37	if layer_idx < starting_layer:
38	    return flash_attn_func(q, k, v, causal=True)   # 浅层 dense
39	else:
40	    return tri_shape_kernel(q, k, v, prefill_kwargs)  # 深层 Triangle
41	```
42	
43	**没有 per-head 切分**——同 layer 内所有 head 走同一 pattern，避开 tensor parallelism imbalance。
44	
45	`tri_mix_minference_forward` 是叠加版本：浅层走 minference_prefill_forward（A-shape / Vertical-Slash / Block-Sparse 三 pattern dynamic），深层走 Triangle。
46	
47	## 3. 关键超参 & 模型差异
48	
49	| 模型 | 总层 | `starting_layer` | Triangle 层数比例 |
50	|---|---|---|---|
51	| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 32 | 16 | 50% |
52	| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-262K | 32 | 16 | 50% |
53	| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 28 | 20 | 28.6% |
54	
55	固定参数：`n_init=8, n_local=512, n_last=128`。Qwen sparse 程度低于 Llama，paper 称"inherent sparsity 不同"，需要每个 model 自己 calibrate。
56	
57	## 4. Layer selection 怎么得到
58	
59	**Gradient probe**（paper Section 2.4 + Appendix）：
60	
61	- 引入 mask 变量 θ_{l,i,j}，初始化为 1，element-wise 乘到 softmax 后的 attention score 上
62	- 计算 `Grad(M, l) = Σ ∂y_gt/∂θ_{l,i,j} / |M|`（y_gt 是 ground truth logit）
63	- 在 middle Q-K 区域 mask（即 sink + window + last 之外的 block）
64	- 用 ~2000 token 的 KV retrieval 任务、100 个样本测
65	- 取 contribution 最低的 L_tri 个 layer 走 Triangle
66	
67	实际操作上 paper 用的不是按 contribution 单独选层（散点），而是 contiguous "starting_layer 之后所有层走 Triangle"——README 描述为 "applies dense attention in shallow layers, switches to triangle in deeper layers"。
68	
69	## 5. 实测数据
70	
71	### Accuracy（RULER 128K, Llama-3.1-8B, A100）
72	
73	| Method | AVG | NIAH.SG1 | NIAH.MK3 | VT | **CWE** | FWE | QA1 |
74	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
75	| Dense | 77.6 | 100.0 | 62.0 | 90.0 | **2.2** | 57.33 | 77.0 |
76	| TriangleMix (L_tri=16) | 77.3 | 100.0 | 63.0 | 93.2 | **0.0** | 50.67 | 77.0 |
77	
78	⚠️ **CWE 2.2 → 0.0**：paper 也承认（Section 5），但 dense 本身只有 2.2 ≈ 噪声，差距小。
79	⚠️ **FWE 57.3 → 50.7**（频繁词提取，-6.6 点）。
80	✅ NIAH / QA 几乎无损。
81	
82	### TTFT（Llama-3.1-8B, A100）
83	
84	| 长度 | Dense | MInference | **TriangleMix** | Ours+MInference |
85	|---|---|---|---|---|
86	| 32K | 4.1s | 5.5s (+34%) | **3.6s (−12%)** | 4.2s (+2%) |
87	| 48K | 7.3s | 7.8s (+7%) | **5.9s (−19%)** | 6.0s (−18%) |
88	| 64K | 11.2s | 10.1s (−10%) | 8.6s (−23%) | **7.7s (−31%)** |
89	| 80K | 15.9s | 12.3s (−23%) | 11.7s (−26%) | **9.5s (−40%)** |
90	| 96K | 21.3s | 13.4s (−37%) | 15.2s (−29%) | **10.9s (−49%)** |
91	| 128K | 34.5s | 18.0s (−48%) | 23.4s (−32%) | **14.5s (−58%)** |
92	
93	短 ctx（32–48K）单独 TriangleMix 比 MInference 强；128K MInference 反超。叠加版本几乎全段最优。
94	
95	### Attention kernel 单段 latency（128K）
96	
97	| Kernel | Latency |
98	|---|---|
99	| Dense | 750 ms |
100	| MInference | 229 ms (3.3×) |
101	| FlexPrefill | 220 ms (3.4×) |
102	| **Triangle** | **49 ms (15.3×)** |
103	
104	Triangle 加速远高于 dynamic sparse 方法。
105	
106	## 6. Limitation（paper Section 5 + README）
107	
108	1. **CWE/FWE 类提取式任务**：sparse 损失明显（middle Q-K 也重要）
109	2. **Inherent sparsity 跟模型有关**：Qwen 显著低于 Llama
110	3. **Train-Test Misalignment hypothesis**：训练时 loss 对所有位置均匀，推理只关心 prompt 之后，所以"middle Q-K 在深层只对预测 prompt 内部的 token 有用，对 generation 没意义"——这是 Triangle 设计的理论依据
111	4. **PassageRetrieval shallow layer** 走 Triangle 会掉点（README 提到 "shallow layer attention over Middle Q-K remains crucial for retrieval"）
112	
113	## 7. 上游代码结构
114	
115	```
116	third_party/MInference/TriangleMix/           # paper repo 子目录
117	├── README.md
118	├── speed_test.py            # TTFT 测试脚本
119	├── setup_ruler.sh
120	└── ruler/                   # RULER 评测 wiring (vLLM / TRT-LLM)
121	```
122	
123	实际算法实现在父目录 `third_party/MInference/minference/` 下：
124	
125	```
126	minference/
127	├── modules/
128	│   ├── tri_mix.py                       # 54 行 dispatch
129	│   ├── minference_forward.py            # dynamic sparse (A-shape/V-S/Block)
130	│   └── flexprefill.py
131	└── ops/
132	    └── streaming_kernel.py              # 839 行 Triton FA-2 with sink+window
133	        ├── _attn_fwd_inner (line 26)    # FA-2 inner loop with sliding window
134	        ├── _attn_fwd (line 116)         # autotuned outer kernel
135	        ├── _forward (line ~360)         # python wrapper
136	        ├── TritonMultiStageDotProductionAttention (line 531)
137	        │   ├── append()                 # 多段 KV 增量 softmax
138	        │   └── finalize()
139	        └── a_shape_kernel (line 781)    # sink+window 简单封装
140	        └── tri_shape_kernel (line 820)  # 上面公式
141	```
142	
143	## 8. 跟 InfLLM-v2 关系
144	
145	- **概念正交**：InfLLM-v2 是 block-level dynamic top-K（query 选 K block）；Triangle 是 token-level 静态 pattern（sink + window + last，不看 query 内容）
146	- **训练假设不同**：InfLLM-v2 是 training-aware（model weight 学过 block-sparse 行为）；Triangle 是 training-free
147	- **可叠加方式**：浅层 std layer 走 InfLLM-v2 sparse，深层 std layer 走 Triangle（类似 paper 的 `tri_mix_minference_forward` 但 InfLLM-v2 换 MInference 的位置）
148	
149	## 9. 跟 SGLang paged-KV 的差距
150	
151	上游实现假设 `(B, H, N, D)` dense tensor。SGLang 是 paged-KV：
152	
153	- KV cache 存为 `(num_pages, page_size, H_kv, D)`
154	- 通过 `req_to_token[req_pool_idx, :kv_len]` 拿到 page slot indices
155	- 真正读 KV 要 `key_cache[slots]` gather
156	
157	→ 集成时需要在 Triangle dispatch path 加一层 paged → dense gather。本仓 `_verify_manual_sdpa_with_mask`（minicpm_backend.py:980）已有现成 gather 实现可参考。
158

```
# Core Research Method and Findings

**Core Method:**
The researchers employ "entropy-based top-k sparsification" to systematically ablate attention heads while preserving the most informative ones. They calculate entropy of attention weight distributions and retain only the k heads exhibiting the lowest entropy (most focused patterns), testing this across sparsification levels.

**Hybrid Model Applicability:**
The study examines three hybrid SSM-Transformer architectures: RecurrentGemma-2B (10 heads), RecurrentGemma-9B (16 heads), and Jamba-Mini-1.6 (32 heads). Findings demonstrate consistent functional segregation across models with varying attention layer densities and organization patterns.

**NIAH Preservation:**
Yes. The research shows that "sparsifying to just 15% of attention heads maintains near-perfect retrieval" on the Needle-In-A-Haystack benchmark while preserving 84% of MMLU performance, indicating retrieval capability survives aggressive sparsification.

**Training-Free Approach:**
Correct. All experiments involve post-hoc manipulation of pretrained models without retraining, using inference-time modifications through their ManipuLatte library.

**Models Tested:**
Three models representing diverse architectural approaches were evaluated: RecurrentGemma-2B, RecurrentGemma-9B, and Jamba-Mini-1.6, enabling validation across different scales and hybrid design strategies.
```

```
I found comprehensive information about MInference 1.0. Here are the key details:

## Overview

MInference (Milliontokens Inference) is a sparse calculation method designed to accelerate pre-filling of long-sequence processing.

## Hybrid Attention Head Patterns

The method identifies three unique patterns in long-context attention matrices: the A-shape, Vertical-Slash, and Block-Sparse patterns that can be leveraged for efficient sparse computation on GPUs. The optimal pattern for each attention head is determined offline and sparse indices are dynamically built based on the assigned pattern during inference.

## Sparse Prefill Mechanism

With the pattern and sparse indices, efficient sparse attention calculations are performed via optimized GPU kernels to significantly reduce the latency in the pre-filling stage of long-context LLMs.

## Evaluation Results

By evaluating on a wide range of downstream tasks, including InfiniteBench, RULER, PG-19, and Needle In A Haystack (NIAH), and models including LLaMA-3-1M, GLM4-1M, Yi-200K, Phi-3-128K, and Qwen2-128K, MInference effectively reduces inference latency by up to 10x for pre-filling on an A100, while maintaining accuracy.

## Key Technical Features

The proposed technique can be directly applied to existing LLMs without any modifications to the pre-training setup or additional fine-tuning.

The paper was published on arXiv as 2407.02490 in July 2024.
```

40	## TL;DR
41	
42	**MInference 1.0** leverages the dynamic sparse nature of LLMs' attention, which exhibits some static patterns, to speed up the pre-filling for long-context LLMs. It first determines offline which sparse pattern each head belongs to, then approximates the sparse index online and dynamically computes attention with the optimal custom kernels. This approach achieves up to a **10x speedup** for pre-filling on an A100 while maintaining accuracy.
43	
44	- [MInference 1.0: Accelerating Pre-filling for Long-Context LLMs via Dynamic Sparse Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02490) (NeurIPS'24 **spotlight**, ES-FoMo @ ICML'24)<br>
45	  _Huiqiang Jiang†, Yucheng Li†, Chengruidong Zhang†, Qianhui Wu, Xufang Luo, Surin Ahn, Zhenhua Han, Amir H. Abdi, Dongsheng Li, Chin-Yew Lin, Yuqing Yang and Lili Qiu_
46	
47	**SCBench** analyzes long-context methods from a **KV cache-centric perspective** across the full KV cache lifecycle (e.g., KV cache generation, compression, retrieval, and loading). It evaluates 12 tasks under two shared context modes, covering four categories of long-context capabilities: string retrieval, semantic retrieval, global information, and multi-task scenarios.
48	
49	- [SCBench: A KV Cache-Centric Analysis of Long-Context Methods](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10319) (ICLR'25, ENLSP @ NeurIPS'24)<br>
50	  _Yucheng Li, Huiqiang Jiang, Qianhui Wu, Xufang Luo, Surin Ahn, Chengruidong Zhang, Amir H. Abdi, Dongsheng Li, Jianfeng Gao, Yuqing Yang and Lili Qiu_
51	
52	**MMInference** use **modality-aware permutation sparse attention** to accelerate long-context VLMs inference in prefilling-stage. Specifically, we implement three distinct permutation-based sparse attention mechanisms, with FlashAttention, FlashDecoding and PIT, to address the grid patterns in vision inputs and the modality boundary issues in mixed-modality scenarios.
53	
54	- [MMInference: Accelerating Pre-filling for Long-Context VLMs via Modality-Aware Permutation Sparse Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16083) (ICML'25, FM-Wild @ ICLR'25)<br>
55	  _Yucheng Li, Huiqiang Jiang, Chengruidong Zhang, Qianhui Wu, Xufang Luo, Surin Ahn, Amir H. Abdi, Dongsheng Li, Jianfeng Gao, Yuqing Yang and Lili Qiu_

64	## 🎯 Quick Start
65	
66	### Requirements
67	
68	- Torch
69	- FlashAttention-2 (Optional)
70	- Triton
71	- **Transformers >= 4.46.0**
72	
73	To get started with MInference, simply install it using pip:
74	
75	```bash
76	pip install minference
77	```
78	
79	### Supported Efficient Methods
80	
81	You can get the complete list of supported efficient methods by running the following code:
82	```python
83	from minference import MInferenceConfig
84	supported_attn_types = MInferenceConfig.get_available_attn_types()
85	supported_kv_types = MInferenceConfig.get_available_kv_types()
86	```
87	
88	Currently, we support the following long-context methods:
89	
90	- **[① KV Cache Generation]:** [MInference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02490), [xAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16428), [FlexPrefill](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20766), [A-shape](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453), [Tri-shape](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10319), [MInference w/ static](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02490), [Dilated](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.05150), [Strided](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10509)
91	- **[② KV Cache Compression]:** [StreamingLLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453), [SnapKV](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14469), [PyramidKV](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02069), [KIVI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02750)
92	- **[③ KV Cache Retrieval]:** [CacheBlend](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16444)
93	- **[④ KV Cache Loading]:** [Quest](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10774), [RetrievalAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10516)
94	
95	For more details about the KV cache lifecycle, please refer to [**SCBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10319). Note that some modes are supported by vLLM, while all modes are supported by HF.
96	
97	### Supported Models
98	
99	General *MInference* **supports any decoding LLMs**, including LLaMA-style models, and Phi models.
100	We have adapted nearly all open-source long-context LLMs available in the market.

```
5	import math

8	import torch
9	import triton
10	import triton.language as tl
11	from einops import rearrange
12	
13	try:
14	    from flash_attn import flash_attn_func
15	except ImportError:
16	    from ..ops.flash_attn_triton import _flash_attn_triton_decoding as flash_attn_func
17	
18	
19	def torch_block_wise_attention(
20	    q: torch.Tensor,
21	    k: torch.Tensor,
22	    v: torch.Tensor,
23	    block_idx: torch.Tensor,
24	    block_size: int,
25	    grid_offset: int = 0,
26	):
27	    b, n, h, d = q.shape
28	    assert k.shape == q.shape
29	    assert v.shape == k.shape
30	    num_block = math.ceil(grid_offset / block_size) + math.ceil(
31	        (n - grid_offset) / block_size
32	    )
33	    # get topk block idx and build mask
34	    mask = torch.zeros(b, h, num_block, num_block, dtype=torch.bool, device=q.device)
35	    mask[
36	        torch.arange(b).view(b, 1, 1).expand(b, h, block_idx.shape[-1]),
37	        torch.arange(h).view(1, h, 1).expand(b, h, block_idx.shape[-1]),
38	        block_idx // num_block,
39	        block_idx % num_block,
40	    ] = 1
41	    act_blocks_per_row = torch.tril(mask).sum(-1)
42	    mask = mask.repeat_interleave(block_size, -2).repeat_interleave(block_size, -1)
43	    mask = mask[..., grid_offset : grid_offset + n, grid_offset : grid_offset + n]
44	    mask = torch.tril(mask)
45	    attn_weight = torch.einsum("bihd,bjhd->bhij", q, k) / math.sqrt(d)
46	    attn_weight.masked_fill_(~mask, float("-inf"))
47	    attn_weight = torch.softmax(attn_weight, dim=-1)
48	    o = torch.einsum("bhij,bjhd->bhid", attn_weight, v)
49	    o = o.transpose(1, 2)
50	    return o
```

> DEVELOPER

Background: I tried TriangleMix (static sink+sliding-window+last-N causal pattern) on MiniCPM-SALA hybrid (8 std attention + 24 linear/GLA layers). It failed: niah dropped 1.00→0.33 when applied to just 2 std layers. The static pattern is the problem — different queries need different K positions, but Triangle forces every query to see only sink+window+last-128. NIAH needles in the middle are simply masked out for every query.

Mission — find training-free DYNAMIC sparse attention methods for prefill where the K-selection is query-dependent (not a static pattern):

Specifically look for methods that:
1. At prefill time, for each query token (or chunk), DYNAMICALLY select which K positions to attend to
2. Don't require retraining (key constraint)
3. Have working Triton/CUDA kernels for long context (≥128K)
4. Show reproducible NIAH/RULER results

Papers to dig into:
- **MInference 1.0** (Microsoft, arXiv 2407.02490, NeurIPS 2024): the "vertical-slash" pattern is dynamic — picks K positions based on query similarity to recent queries. Per-head pattern selection.
- **MInference 1.5 / MMInference** (2024-2025): updates to v1
- **FlexPrefill** (ByteDance, arXiv 2502.20766, ICLR 2025): per-head per-query budget allocation, claims NIAH preservation at long context
- **SeerAttention** (Liu et al., arXiv 2410.13276): learnable mask, training-free variant via attention pooling
- **Quest** (MIT, ICML 2024, arXiv 2406.10774): query-aware page selection — primarily for decode but check if prefill works
- **TidalDecode** (Yang et al., arXiv 2410.05076): block-level dynamic sparsity
- **HSPrune / HSPA** (recent NeurIPS submissions): hierarchical sparse prefill
- **Native Sparse Attention (NSA)** by DeepSeek (arXiv 2502.11089): training-time but check if "inference-time NSA" exists as a knob — i.e. apply NSA pattern offline-calibrated
- **MoBA** (Kimi/Moonshot, 2025): training-time but inference-time variants?
- **Star Attention** (NVIDIA, arXiv 2411.17116): partition-then-combine for distributed prefill — different angle
- **InfLLM** (Tsinghua, arXiv 2402.04617): block-level training-free retrieval — predecessor of what we already run as baseline (InfLLM-v2)
- **HiP-Attention** (DeepAuto, 2024): hierarchical pruning, recursive
- **A-Shape / Pyramid Inference** style approaches

For each, report:
1. **arXiv + lab + year**
2. **Selection mechanism** — what signal drives K selection at runtime? (query-K cosine? attention score from a low-rank proxy? sketched attention? KV mean pooling per chunk?)
3. **Granularity**: per-token, per-chunk, per-page, per-head
4. **Training-free?** (must-have)
5. **Reproducible kernel?** github link + activity
6. **NIAH 128K numbers** (claimed)
7. **Will it work on hybrid models?** Most assume full-attention stacks — does the method specifically depend on patterns only present in full-attention?
8. **Already implemented in SGLang or vLLM?** (matters for production)

Compare each method's selection mechanism to InfLLM-v2 (compress_k via average pooling per block → top-K block-level → sparse stage2). What's different/better? The baseline InfLLM-v2 already does dynamic top-K per query at chunk granularity. So we need something materially better than that.

CRITICAL — note that our baseline ALREADY uses InfLLM-v2 sparse stage2 at ctx≥16K. So any new method needs to either:
(a) Be cheaper than InfLLM-v2 with similar accuracy, OR
(b) Be more accurate (higher NIAH retention) so we can be more aggressive (smaller dense_len threshold, fewer keep-tokens, etc.)

If you find that most dynamic sparse methods are "similar idea, slight variant of top-K block selection" and InfLLM-v2 already covers that design space, say so — we may need to stop looking and accept the current sparse stack is near the training-free Pareto frontier.

DO NOT WRITE CODE. Report only. Be quantitative — show numbers, not just method names. 1500-2500 words covering 6-10 methods in depth.

```
# MInference on Hybrid Models and Attention Patterns

## Models Tested

The paper focuses on traditional transformer-based LLMs. Testing included "LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct-262k, GLM-4-9B-1M, and Yi-9B-200K" plus Phi-3 and Qwen2 variants. There is **no explicit discussion of hybrid architectures** like GLA+attention or Mamba+attention hybrids.

## NIAH Retrieval Performance

Yes, MInference preserves needle-in-haystack retrieval capability. Figure 1a demonstrates the method "matches or surpasses baselines" on this task across 1M-token contexts, and results show "100.0" scores on PassKey retrieval tasks in Table 2.

## Pattern Origins Discussion

The paper provides **limited mechanistic explanation** for why these patterns emerge. It notes that "attention distributions vary significantly across different inputs" and demonstrates spatial clustering through empirical observation. However, it does **not theoretically explain** whether patterns depend on having dense attention layers or would persist in sparse-only architectures.

The authors mention in Appendix G that they investigated whether patterns exist "only in Auto-Regressive LLMs or RoPE-Based LLMs?" but the actual content of that section is truncated in the provided text.

**Conclusion:** The work assumes standard transformer architectures and doesn't address how architectural changes like reducing attention layers would affect sparse pattern formation.
```

```
Based on the search results, I found several relevant papers on arXiv from 2025 related to sparse attention, KV cache, and hybrid models:

## Key Findings

**Quest - Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference:**
Quest is a block-wise dynamic sparse attention method focusing on decoding. Quest uses a block size of 16 by default and keeps the first two layers fully dense to minimize error.

**Hybrid Models and Head-Based Optimization:**
Not all heads require top-k selection and the subsequent attention computation; only retrieval heads require joint optimization of selection granularity and KV budget. HybridKV leverages head-level attention patterns to classify static and dynamic heads via text-guided signals, enabling hierarchical budget allocation with tailored pruning and retrieval strategies.

**Recent Hybrid Sparse Attention Work (2025):**
Fluxion combines output-aware KV budgeting, head-specific and granularity-aware sparse configuration, and cross-device coordinated execution for sparse attention over CPU-resident KV caches. Fluxion preserves quality well with worst average degradation of only -0.26 relative to FULL, while delivering 1.5×-3.7× speedup.

The search results show active research in combining sparse attention mechanisms with KV cache management, head-level classification, and hybrid CPU-GPU approaches for efficient long-context LLM inference in 2025.
```

```
I've performed a web search for your query about FlexPrefill, SeerAttention, TidalDecode, and related hybrid attention mechanisms. Here's what I found:

## Key Findings:

**FlexPrefill:**
FlexPrefill is a Flexible sparse Pre-filling mechanism that dynamically adjusts sparse attention patterns and computational budget in real-time to meet the specific requirements of each input and attention head. FlexPrefill was selected as an Oral Presentation (1.77%) at ICLR 2025, and it further adapts the vertical-slash sparsity ratio dynamically and uses pooled queries and pooled keys to estimate query-aware block-wise patterns.

**SeerAttention:**
SeerAttention is a simple yet effective attention mechanism that directly learns the intrinsic attention sparsity from the LLM itself, without relying on predefined sparsity patterns. SeerAttention achieves highly linear speedup over dense configurations, delivering a 7.3× speedup with 90% sparsity on sequences of 128k. SeerAttention introduces self-distilled Attention Gate (AttnGate) that dynamically activates sparse blocks in attention computation for efficient long-context prefilling.

**TidalDecode:**
TidalDecode can consistently outperform full attention baseline and Quest by a large margin under all token budgets and context lengths through token pattern reuse to minimize the token selection overhead. TidalDecode performs full attention for the initial Transformer layers, then performs full attention with token selection for specific layers, and finally performs position persistent sparse attention where only selected tokens are loaded from the KV cache.

**Hybrid Models:**
Efficient sequence modeling alternatives include state space models, linear attention variants, and recurrent architectures, and to balance efficiency and expressiveness, hybrid architectures have emerged that interleave full attention with these efficient alternatives.
```

```
252:        return block_sparse_attention(q, k, v, topk)
258:    for ty, fc in [("stream_llm", streaming_forward), ("vertical_and_slash", vertical_and_slash_kernel), ("block_sparse", block_sparse_kernel)]:
261:        elif ty == "vertical_and_slash":
296:def gather_last_q_vertical_slash_topk_v4(self, q, k, v, head_id):
298:    def vertical_and_slash(attn_weights, vertical_size, slash_size):
301:        vertical_size, slash_size  = min(q_len, max(vertical_size, 30)), min(q_len, max(slash_size, 50))
305:        vertical = qk.sum(-2, keepdim=True)
306:        vertical[...,:30] = -self.ne_inf
307:        vertical_topk = torch.topk(-vertical, q_len - vertical_size, -1).indices
317:        est_attn = est_attn.scatter(3, vertical_topk.expand(*est_attn.shape[:dim], vertical_topk.shape[dim], *est_attn.shape[dim + 1 :]), 0)
325:            self.vertical = torch.topk(vertical, vertical_size * 4, -1).indices
329:    def stream_llm(attn_weights, vertical_size, slash_size):
331:        vertical_size, slash_size = min(q_len, max(vertical_size, 30)), min(q_len, max(slash_size, 50))
```

```
32	    Single-kernel implementation that fuses k computation, key compression,
33	    key_cache write, and full_compressed_k read for ALL chunks (history + new).
34	
35	    Grid: (batch_size, min(max_total_chunks, max_grid_chunks), head_num_k)
36	    where max_total_chunks = max_chunks_per_seq + max_history_chunks
37	    - chunk_in_seq in [0, history_chunks_in_seq): process HISTORY chunks
38	    - chunk_in_seq in [history_chunks_in_seq, total_chunks_in_seq): process NEW chunks
39	    
40	    If total_chunks > max_grid_chunks, each thread block loops to handle multiple chunks.
41

43	    Only head=0 threads write to key_cache or full_compressed_k to avoid redundant writes.

49	        history_compress_k_token_nums_ptr: History compressed token nums [batch_size]

63	        kernel_stride: Stride between chunk starts
64	        BLOCK_SIZE: Vectorized load/store width
65	        max_grid_chunks: Maximum grid dimension for chunks (kernel loops if more chunks needed)
66	    """
67	    batch_idx = tl.program_id(0)
68	    grid_chunk_idx = tl.program_id(1)
```

1	# 集成设计
2	
3	## 总体策略
4	
5	1. **新增 Triangle path，不替换 InfLLM-v2 sparse**。Triangle layer 独立 dispatch，其余 std layer 保留 InfLLM-v2 sparse / dense FA 路径
6	2. **Triangle layer 集合由 gradient probe 决定**（P1 输出），不预设拍脑袋数字
7	3. **永远启用 Triangle**：不区分 NO_SPEC vs spec batch，EAGLE aux layer 22 也可走 Triangle（draft 可重训作为后续任务）
8	4. **Range gate**：仅 `max(seq_lens) >= SGLANG_TRIANGLEMIX_MIN_CTX`（默认 16K）启用
9	5. **Mode gate**：仅 prefill EXTEND mode，bypass `is_target_verify()` / decode
10	6. **不动 GLA layer**（24 个），不动 KV write-in，不动 EAGLE verify path
11	
12	## 端到端调用链
13	
14	```
15	sglang forward → minicpm.py:MiniCPMAttention.forward()
16	                    ├─ qkv_proj
17	                    ├─ rope
18	                    └─ RadixAttention.forward(q, k, v, forward_batch)
19	                              ↓ (forward_batch.attn_backend)
20	                       hybrid_linear_attn_backend.forward_extend
21	                              ↓ (full_attn_backend)
22	                       minicpm_backend.MiniCPMSparseBackend.forward_extend  ← Triangle dispatch 加在这里
23	                          ├─ save_kv_cache (KV 写入 paged pool，不动)
24	                          ├─ if Triangle 条件:
25	                          │     return self._forward_extend_trianglemix(...)
26	                          ├─ elif is_target_verify: ... (EAGLE verify path)
27	                          ├─ elif max_seqlen < dense_len: dense FA path (FlashInfer)
28	                          └─ else: InfLLM-v2 sparse path (compress_k → stage1 → stage2)
29	```
30	
31	## Triangle path 内部
32	
33	```python
34	def _forward_extend_trianglemix(self, q, k, v, layer, forward_batch):
35	    """
36	    每 seq 独立处理。chunked prefill 下：
37	      - 非末 chunk: 所有 q 走 a_shape (sink + sliding window)
38	      - 末 chunk : q[:-n_last] 走 a_shape, q[-n_last:] 跟整段 K dense
39	    """
40	    bs = forward_batch.batch_size
41	    H_q = layer.tp_q_head_num
42	    H_kv = layer.tp_k_head_num
43	    D = layer.head_dim
44	    group = H_q // H_kv  # 16
45	
46	    # 读 paged KV (入口 save_kv_cache 已写)
47	    key_cache_raw, value_cache_raw = forward_batch.token_to_kv_pool.get_kv_buffer(layer.layer_id)
48	    key_cache = key_cache_raw.view(-1, self.page_size, H_kv, D)
49	    value_cache = value_cache_raw.view(-1, self.page_size, H_kv, D)
50	    k_pool = key_cache.squeeze(1)  # (num_pages, H_kv, D)  假设 page_size=1
51	    v_pool = value_cache.squeeze(1)
52	
53	    # CPU 端 metadata
54	    seq_lens_cpu = forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu.tolist()
55	    extend_seq_lens_cpu = forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu.tolist()
56	    extend_prefix_lens_cpu = forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens_cpu.tolist()
57	
58	    q_reshaped = q.contiguous().view(-1, H_q, D)
59	    output = torch.empty_like(q_reshaped)
60	
61	    q_offset = 0
62	    for b in range(bs):
63	        kv_len     = seq_lens_cpu[b]                # 含本 chunk 后的总 KV
64	        ext_len    = extend_seq_lens_cpu[b]         # 本 chunk q 长度
65	        prefix_len = extend_prefix_lens_cpu[b]      # 本 chunk 之前的 KV
66	        is_last_chunk = (prefix_len + ext_len == kv_len)
67	        rpi = int(forward_batch.req_pool_indices[b].item())
68	
69	        # Gather paged KV → 连续 (kv_len, H_kv, D)
70	        slots = self.req_to_token[rpi, :kv_len].to(torch.long)
71	        k_b = k_pool[slots]
72	        v_b = v_pool[slots]
73	        if is_fp8_kv:
74	            k_b = (k_b.to(torch.float32) * k_scale_float).to(q.dtype)
75	            v_b = (v_b.to(torch.float32) * v_scale_float).to(q.dtype)
76	
77	        # GQA expand → (kv_len, H_q, D)
78	        if group > 1:
79	            k_b = k_b.repeat_interleave(group, dim=1)
80	            v_b = v_b.repeat_interleave(group, dim=1)
81	
82	        # 排成 Triton kernel 期望的 (1, H_q, N, D)
83	        k_b = k_b.permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(0).contiguous()
84	        v_b = v_b.permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(0).contiguous()
85	
86	        q_b = q_reshaped[q_offset : q_offset + ext_len]
87	        q_b = q_b.permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(0).contiguous()  # (1, H_q, ext_len, D)
88	
89	        if is_last_chunk and ext_len > self._tri_n_last:
90	            n_last = self._tri_n_last
91	            # 切 q：前段走 a_shape，末段走 dense
92	            q1, q2 = q_b[:, :, :-n_last], q_b[:, :, -n_last:]
93	            # q1 看到的 K 只到 kv_len - n_last（prompt 末段 K 不可见）
94	            k1 = k_b[:, :, : kv_len - n_last]
95	            v1 = v_b[:, :, : kv_len - n_last]
96	
97	            y1 = a_shape_attn(q1, k1, v1,
98	                              n_init=self._tri_n_init,
99	                              n_local=self._tri_n_local,
100	                              sm_scale=layer.scaling)
101	            # q2 跟完整 K dense；causal mask 在 q2 vs K[-n_last:] 之间
102	            y2 = dense_attn_with_last_causal(q2, k_b, v_b,
103	                                              n_last=n_last,
104	                                              sm_scale=layer.scaling)
105	            y = torch.cat([y1, y2], dim=2)
106	        else:
107	            # 非末 chunk 或末 chunk 太短：全 a_shape
108	            y = a_shape_attn(q_b, k_b, v_b,
109	                             n_init=self._tri_n_init,
110	                             n_local=self._tri_n_local,
111	                             sm_scale=layer.scaling)
112	
113	        # (1, H_q, ext_len, D) → (ext_len, H_q, D)
114	        y = y.squeeze(0).permute(1, 0, 2).contiguous()
115	        output[q_offset : q_offset + ext_len] = y.to(q.dtype)
116	        q_offset += ext_len
117	
118	    return output.view(-1, H_q * D)
119	```

121	## Triton kernel 接口
122	
123	放进 `demo-sala/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trianglemix_kernel.py`：
124	
125	```python
126	def a_shape_attn(q, k, v, n_init: int, n_local: int, sm_scale: float) -> torch.Tensor:
127	    """
128	    Sink + sliding window attention.
129	    q/k/v: (B, H, N, D). 返回 (B, H, N_q, D).
130	    q 看到 K[:n_init] (sink) + K[-n_local:] 内的滑窗。
131	    """
132	
133	def dense_attn_with_last_causal(q2, k, v, n_last: int, sm_scale: float) -> torch.Tensor:
134	    """
135	    q2: (B, H, n_last, D)
136	    k, v: (B, H, N_full, D)
137	    q2 跟完整 K attend；causal mask 仅在 q2 vs K[-n_last:] 之间，
138	    K[:-n_last] 对 q2 完全可见。
139	    n_last=128 不需要 Triton kernel，PyTorch matmul + softmax + matmul 即可。
140	    """
141	```
142	
143	来源：`third_party/MInference/minference/ops/streaming_kernel.py`
144	- `_attn_fwd_inner` / `_attn_fwd` (Triton FA-2 with sliding window)
145	- `TritonMultiStageDotProductionAttention.append/finalize`
146	- `a_shape_kernel`（包装上面三个）
147	
148	## 关键正确性陷阱
149	
150	| 陷阱 | 说明 |
151	|---|---|
152	| q2 看到的 K 范围 | 是整段 K，**不只是 K 末段**。paper 的 dense 是 "q2 跟全部 K attend"，causal 只 mask q2 vs K 末 n_last 之间 |
153	| q1 看到的 K 范围 | 是 `K[:-n_last]`（前段 K），不包含 prompt 末 n_last。q1 完全感知不到 prompt 末段 |
154	| chunked 末段语义 | 仅"本 chunk 末尾恰是 prompt 末尾"才切 q2；其他 chunk 全走 a_shape。靠 `prefix_len + ext_len == seq_lens[b]` 判断 |
155	| sink 区域大小 | n_init=8 是 token 级，不是 page 级 |
156	| sliding window 对齐 | a_shape_kernel 内 window 是"最近 n_local 个 K"；当 q1 看到的 K 是 K[:-n_last]，window 是 K[-n_last - n_local : -n_last] |
157	| GQA repeat 显存 | H_q=32, H_kv=2, group=16。expand 后 (kv_len, 32, 128) 显存 4× per seq per layer。单 seq 处理后立即释放，不要 batch 累积 |
158	| FP8 KV dequant | 走现有 `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float`。KV cache dtype 看 `--kv-cache-dtype`（本仓提交包默认 bf16） |
159	| KV 读取在 save_kv_cache 之后 | save_kv_cache 在 forward_extend 入口就执行，Triangle 计算时 cache 已包含本 chunk K |
160	| 不能污染 sparse metadata | Triangle layer skip sparse path，但要确认不动 `metadata.sparse_*` in-place state（P3 grep 审计） |
161	
162	## Metadata 共享审计
163	
164	`self.forward_metadata` 一次性建好所有 layer 共享。InfLLM-v2 sparse layer 在 forward_extend 中 in-place 写 `metadata.sparse_page_table` (line 1947-1949)。
165	
166	- 每个 sparse layer 自己重新算 topk + 重写 sparse_page_table → 跨 layer 不依赖前面 layer 的写入
167	- `metadata.k1`, `metadata.k2`（compress_k 输出）在 forward_metadata_init 一次性算好，不 per-layer 重算
168	- Triangle layer 跳过 sparse path 不读不写 `metadata.sparse_*` → **不污染**
169	
170	P3 实施前需要 grep 一次 `metadata\.[a-z_]+\s*=` 全部 in-place 写入点确认。
171	
172	## EAGLE-3 兼容
173	
174	```python
175	if layer.layer_id in self._triangle_layers \
176	   and max_kv >= self._tri_min_ctx \
177	   and not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_target_verify() \
178	   and forward_batch.forward_mode.is_extend():
179	    return self._forward_extend_trianglemix(...)
180	```
181	
182	- **target verify path 不动**（line 1754 `is_target_verify()`）：走原 wrapper / sparse / manual SDPA。Triangle 不入侵 verify
183	- **prefill EXTEND 永远启用 Triangle**（包括 spec mode 的 target prefill）。target hidden states 改变 → 影响 KV cache → spec verify accept rate 下降。**接受这个退化**（draft 可重训作后续任务）

229	- gla_qkv_split_ms 0 (contig copy 完全消失 vs §2.12 的 8.74ms)

234	### 2.14 GLA fused o_norm + sigmoid + mul (3-in-1 triton)
235	
236	代码：`demo-sala/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/minicpm.py::_minicpm_gla_rmsnorm_sigmoid_mul`
237	
238	| env | 默认 |
239	|---|---:|
240	| `SGLANG_MINICPM_GLA_FUSED_RMSNORM_SIGMOID_MUL` | `1` （已默认开启） |
241	| `SGLANG_MINICPM_GLA_FUSED_SIGMOID_MUL` | `0` （仅 sigmoid+mul 子集，被本条覆盖） |
242	
243	替代：
244	```python
245	# 原: 3 kernel
246	o = self.o_norm(o)        # sgl_kernel.rmsnorm
247	z = self.z_proj(...)
248	o = o * F.sigmoid(z)      # 2 kernels: sigmoid + mul
249	```
250	
251	合一 triton kernel 全 fp32 计算：
252	```
253	m[i,j] = o[i,j] * rstd[i] * w[j] * sigmoid(z[i,j])
254	```
255	重排安全：z_proj 只依赖 hidden_states，与 o 独立。
256	
257	数值：
258	- microbench (M=8192, H=4096, BLOCK_M=4 num_warps=4) ref 225us → 156us / call
259	- vs ref: 2 bf16 ULP（fp32 全程比 baseline 的 bf16 中间 cast 更精确方向）
260	
261	线上 PROFILE=1：`o_norm 1.96 + sigmoid_mul 2.44 = 4.4 ms` → `o_norm_sigmoid_mul 3.47 ms` (-1ms / chunk)。

277	
278	## 3. 已否决路线
279	
280	每条记录：做了什么 / 为什么失败 / 不要再做什么。
281	
282	### 3.1 fi_convert 跨层缓存
283	
284	旧结论"同 forward 8 层 page table 相同"是错的：tensor 指针相同，但每个 standard layer 都按本层 q/k 重写内容。仅保留 `SGLANG_MINICPM_UNSAFE_FI_CONVERT_CACHE=1` 实验开关，不可线上。
285	
286	### 3.2 TrtLLM stage2 替换
287	
288	长上下文 sparse stage2 实际是 decode-style（`max_seqlen_q==1`）；FlashInfer causal 是 right-aligned，TrtLLM `mask_mode="causal"` 在 `q_len << kv_len` 时语义不等价。HEAD 已不含 `_USE_TRTLLM_STAGE2`。除非先做 right-aligned causal 等价的离线证明，否则不要继续。
289	
290	### 3.3 fast prefill stage1
291	
292	`SGLANG_FAST_PREFILL_STAGE1=1` 默认关闭。当前实现 k1-only 丢 k2 语义，没有完整复现官方 causal/full-layout pooler，topk match 差且不快。
293	
294	### 3.4 compressed maxlen 旧方案
295	
296	不能缩 `max_pooling_1d_varlen.max_context_len` / score full layout。精度根因在 pooler layout/边界语义，topk 放大后会改变 sparse blocks。当前可用的是 §2.5 stage1 actual maxlen + full-layout scratch/direct-pool guard。
297	
298	### 3.5 compressed-K buffer 复用
299	
300	缓存 `compressed_k/k2` 后 `fill_(-inf)` 实测 15chunk 打平（7.609 vs 7.602s），`compress_k_buffer_prefill_ms≈0.03ms/call`。不值得维护成本。
301	
302	### 3.6 `--fuse-topk`
303	
304	global 启用导致 target CUDA graph capture 6.5→14.4s，`decode_topk_ms` 跳到 16ms，运行中触发 CUDA illegal memory access（栈在 FlashInfer decode forward 后 synchronize）。是 decode/verify 路径风险，不是 prefill 优化。
305	
306	prefill-only 复查：`compressed_attention_tilelang` vs `compressed_attention` topk 大面积不匹配（如 `bad_sorted=19315/24576`），TileLang 只吃 `k1` 没复现 `k2/v` 语义。除非重写一个真正复现 stage1+k2 的 kernel，否则禁用。
307	
308	### 3.7 MLP cuDNN（down-only / full-chunk）
309	
310	- down 单独 cudnn：`max_diff=0` 但 `mlp_down_ms` 49→52-56ms（更慢）。
311	- 整 MLP `M=8192` cudnn：`gate/up/down max_diff=0`，但非 power-of-two M 出现明显 diff（`M=2754/6144`），且 `M=8192` e2e `down` 常更慢。
312	- `auto` 后端：tail M 选与 cutlass 不一致路径。
313	
314	不要新增 MLP cuDNN shape gate。
315	
316	### 3.8 stage1 q repeat
317	
318	`current_ratio < 16` 的 q repeat 在生产路径不触发（实测 `q_heads=32 kv_heads=2` ratio=16），跳过 repeat 的开关是 no-op。
319	
320	### 3.9 MLP activation buffer cache
321	
322	给 `SiluAndMul` 输出加全局 buffer，`mlp_act_ms` 不变，wall 无改善，还多占显存。
323	
324	### 3.10 跨层 topk 复用
325	
326	15chunk full chunk 相邻 standard sparse layer `ret` 完全一致率：首个 8K chunk 0.887-0.918，第二个起 0.423-0.476。不是稳定可复用元数据；强行复用是近似注意力语义改动。
327	
328	### 3.11 chunked-prefill-size 16384
329	
330	8192 vs 16384：avg `7.605s` vs `7.751s`。chunk 数从 15 减到 8 但单 chunk 退化抵消调度收益（`extend_sparse_fa` 11-12→23-24ms/层，MLP 150→350ms/chunk，GLA 110→205ms）。
331	
332	### 3.12 FP4 tune cache 补 8192 shapes
333	
334	补 MLP/qkv 完整 chunk shape 后 microbench 小幅改善（`gate_up 3.93→3.89ms`，`std_qkv 0.59→0.55ms`，`max_diff=0`），但真实 15chunk wall 在噪声内。不为此更新提交包 cache。
335	
336	### 3.13 FlashInfer sparse stage2 backend / split-KV 参数
337	
338	- `default(auto)+TC` ≈ `7617us`，`fa2+TC` ≈ `7590us`；`fa2`/`fa3`/`cutlass`/`trtllm-gen` 失败或不支持当前 group/shape。
339	- `use_tensor_cores=False` 不支持 `group_size=16`；`fixed_split_size` 更小需 GB 级 workspace；`disable_split_kv` 更慢。
340	- `flash_attn_with_kvcache` sparse page-table 路径不可用：`Can not import FA3 in sgl_kernel`。
341	- 同 `q_len=1` row 化：decode wrapper 与 prefill wrapper `max_diff=0` 且性能相同，强切 prefill wrapper 无收益。
342	
343	stage2 backend 旋钮已枯竭；要继续必须改 KV/block layout 或写等价 kernel。
344	
345	### 3.14 stage1 mask / dtype 快捷路径
346	
347	- `causal=False`：生产 adjusted-q shape 比 `causal=True` 更慢且 topk 大面积变化（`bad 972658/1572864`）。
348	- 输入转 fp16：速度持平，topk 大面积变化（`bad 1500035/1572864`）。
349	- 真实生产 stage1 不是裸 `q=8192`：wrapper 把 32Q/2KV 的 16 group 展到序列维，C++ 的 `max_seqlen_q_adjusted=131072`。早期 `q=8192,1.7ms` microbench 不是线上形态。
350	- 缩 `max_seqlen_q_adjusted` 到 `min(q*16, k1*16)`：变快但 topk 大面积变化（`k1=4095` bad 777303）。adjusted-q 不是单纯 launch bound，参与 causal/pool 边界语义。
351	- `kBlockN=128` stage1 trait（本地构建）：`10.07→16.40ms`，且 `topk_order_same=0.99485`，已撤回。
352	
353	stage1 高收益路必须改 InfLLM C++/CUDA：把 `hdim16_reduce → score → max_pool → topk` 融合直接产出 pooled/topk，或重写完整等价 kernel；不能做 topk 缩限或候选裁剪。
354	
355	### 3.15 GLA chunk kernel 替换
356	
357	| 路径 | 时间 / 一致性 |
358	|---|---|
359	| `chunk_simple_gla` baseline | `0.60ms`，bitwise OK |
360	| `chunk_size=128` | `0.46ms`，**output max_diff=0.25**（不可用）|
361	| `fused_chunk_simple_gla` | `0.83ms`，**更慢且 output 不一致** |
362	
363	GLA 简单 chunk-size/API 替换不可行。要继续必须写形状特化的等价 kernel 或动 qkv layout（v 非 contig stride）。
364	
365	### 3.16 FP4 input quant 复用 / qkv+gate 融合
366	
367	- input quant 复用：命中一致（`fp4_equal=True`），但 wall 在噪声内。
368	- qkv + output gate FP4 GEMM 融合：`mm_fp4` 只有单个 `alpha`，weight `weight_scale_2` 不同（如 L1 lightning q/k/v `0.0001313` vs `z_proj 0.00015394`），强行合并改 bf16 舍入语义。除非有 per-output alpha 的 GEMM。
369	
370	### 3.17 b12x backend
371	
372	`modelopt_quant.py` 当前未接入 b12x dispatch；`b12x_available()` 可 true 但 JIT 编译失败：`cutlass.utils.HardwareInfo().get_max_active_clusters()` 与当前 cutlass DSL MLIR API 不兼容；绕过后在 MLIR object 处 `abort()`（`Expected an MLIR object ... OpResultList`），不是可捕获异常。撤回了 patch。
373	
374	要重启需先修 cutlass DSL/JIT，再做 decode/no-spec 专项 A/B（不是 prefill 主线）。
375	
376	### 3.18 相邻 topk row 合并 / head_group 共享
377	
378	`SGLANG_MINICPM_PROFILE_TOPK_ADJ=1` profile 真实 line39 第二个 full chunk 起：
379	
380	- 相邻 token `adj_equal`：L0 `0.0414`，其余 sparse layer `0.0001-0.0007`，`mean_run≈1.00, max_run=2`。
381	- 两 head group `head_group_equal`：L0 `0.0013`，其余 `0.0000-0.0010`。
382	
383	不能 exact 合并为 `q_len>1` row，也不能合成共享 page list 的单 wrapper。除非引入近似/per-token mask，方向不可行。
384	
385	### 3.19 stage2 BlockSparse split + LSE merge
386	
387	完整探索（已撤回，备份 `outputs/prefill_experiments/stage2_blocksplit_unlanded.patch`）：
388	
389	- profile 确认第二个 full chunk 起每层 `95 full + 1 partial blocks`。
390	- `BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(R=1,C=64)` 双 head-group forward-only `9.11ms` vs page1 expanded `10.11ms`，离线约 `+10%`；BlockSparse + page64 partial + Triton log2-LSE merge 单 head `4.74→4.95ms`，约 `+4%`，对拍 `cos=0.99999857 max_diff=0.000488`。
391	- 旧 LSE merge 失败原因记录：FlashInfer LSE 是 log2 域，必须用 `2 ** (lse - max_lse)`，不是 `exp`。
392	- gate 唯一可用的是 `metadata.token_pos_in_bs.min() >= topk_tokens`；`extend_prefix_lens_cpu` / `seq_lens_cpu` 都不可靠。
393	- 线上接入 `SGLANG_MINICPM_STAGE2_BLOCKSPLIT=1`：第二 full chunk 命中 split (`use_split=True, offset=63`)，但 `extend_sparse_fa` 没有下降（118.6ms / 后续 82-84ms），no-profile 15chunk avg `7.114s` vs default `7.110s`。
394	
395	离线 `+4%` forward-only 没穿透 wall，`q_h.contiguous()` / 双 wrapper / merge 开销吃光收益。同构 split 接入路线封死，重启必须换 KV/block layout 或单 wrapper / 单 kernel 的完整等价实现。
396	
397	### 3.20 stage2 page64（双 wrapper）
398	
399	`page_size=64` metadata 从 ~384MB 缩到 ~6MB，离线 page1 vs page64 `diff=0`，plan `46.7→19.5ms`，forward `10.04→8.97ms`。但双 wrapper 破坏 single-wrapper plan-cache 路径，每层 `bf≈18-19ms`。补 `SGLANG_MINICPM_PAGE64_PLAN_CACHE=1` 后 microbench `45.77→9.81ms/call`，但真实 15chunk 与 page1 端到端打平。保留 `SGLANG_MINICPM_STAGE2_BLOCK_PAGE64=1` 实验开关默认 `0`。
400	
401	stage2 真正剩余的算法/layout 路径：单 wrapper KV layout 或 custom block-sparse stage2 kernel。
402	
403	### 3.21 Triton 直写 stage2
404	
405	生产近似 `rows=16384, topk=96x64, seq=131072` bf16：`triton_direct=10.37ms` vs FlashInfer forward + `topk_to_fi_indices=10.13ms`，慢 ~2.4%。tile sweep（`NQ=4096` 单 head-group）最佳 Triton `BH16 BN64 W4 2.69ms` vs FlashInfer `2.27ms`，仍慢 18%。简单 streaming-softmax Triton 不能赢 FlashInfer；要继续需要更接近 FlashInfer 的 split/reduce 结构。
406	
407	### 3.22 stage2 kv dtype 校准
408	
409	`bench/infllmv2/bench_stage2_backends.py` 支持 `STAGE2_KV_DTYPE=bf16|fp8`。当前线上是 bf16 KV，生产形态 `default+TC=10.04ms` 与线上 `fw≈9.8-10.0ms/layer` 对齐。**旧 fp8 口径 ~7.6ms 不能再当 baseline**。
410	
411	### 3.23 MLP dense-as-MoE fused path
412	
413	目标：用 FlashInfer `cutlass_fused_moe` 把 dense MLP 当成 1-expert/top1 MoE，覆盖 `gate_up GEMM -> SiLU*mul FP4 quant -> down GEMM` 整段。
414	
415	验证脚本：`bench/kernels/minicpm/bench_mlp_dense_as_moe_fp4.py`。
416	
417	结果：
418	
419	| Shape | baseline | dense-as-MoE | speedup | diff |
420	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
421	| M=512 | 0.235ms | 0.322ms | 0.731x | max=0 |
422	| M=2754 | 2.147ms | 2.157ms | 0.995x | max=0 |
423	| M=8192 | 6.119ms | 6.060ms | 1.010x | max=0 |
424	
425	结论：
426	- 数值链条可行：MiniCPM dense `[gate, up]` 需转成 FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE 期望的 `[up, gate]`，scale 同步交换后 synthetic 对拍 `max_diff=0`。
427	- 收益不足：full chunk 仅 `+1.0%/layer`，折到 32 层约 `1.9ms/chunk`，低于接入复杂度和 MoE route/runner 风险。
428	- 工程风险：首次触发会编译 `/user_4813494d/.cache/flashinfer/0.6.8.post1/120f/cached_ops/fused_moe_120/fused_moe_120.so`（约 84MB，目录约 192MB）。默认并发编译曾 exit 137；`MAX_JOBS=1` 可完成但耗时约 80s。
429	
430	不进生产。真正有价值的 MLP 方向仍是 dense FP4 GEMM 自身 epilogue 融合，避免写出 `gate_up` BF16 中间结果，而不是复用 MoE runner。
431	
432	### 3.24 MLP gate_up epilogue 融合调查
433	
434	当前线上 MLP 路径：
435	
436	```text
437	fp4 gate_up GEMM -> BF16 gate_up [M, 2*inter]
438	BF16 gate_up -> silu(gate)*up + FP4 quant
439	FP4 activation -> fp4 down GEMM
440	```
441	
442	profile 证据（15chunk/full chunk 口径）：
443	
444	- `mlp_gate_up_ms≈85-92ms/chunk`
445	- `mlp_swiglu_fp4_quant_ms≈16.2ms/chunk`
446	- `mlp_down_fp4_quantized_ms≈47-51ms/chunk`
447	- gate_up BF16 中间态约 `8192 * 32768 * 2B = 512MB/chunk`，后续 swiglu+quant 再读一遍。
448	
449	核心收益点不是替换 swiglu 小 kernel，而是让 gate_up GEMM epilogue 直接输出 down_proj 需要的 FP4 activation + scale，消掉 BF16 gate_up 的写回/读回和独立 activation launch。
450	
451	已确认的底层边界：
452	
453	- FlashInfer SM120 FP4 GEMM 生产模板当前 epilogue 是普通 `LinearCombination<OutElementType, float, void, float>`，只输出 BF16/FP16。
454	- CUTLASS SM120 已有 `LinCombBlockScaleFactor` / `LinCombEltActBlockScaleFactor` 和 `Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStore`，支持在 epilogue 生成 FP4 输出和 scale。
455	- 现成 blockscale epilogue是逐元素 unary activation，不能直接表达 SwiGLU 的 pairwise `up * silu(gate)`，也不能把 GEMM 的 `N=2*inter` 存成 `N=inter`。
456	- cuDNN `gemm_swiglu_wrapper_sm100` 和 FlashInfer CuteDSL SM100/103 kernel 语义正确：权重按 `[up32, gate32, ...]` 交错，epilogue 从两个 accumulator subtile 取 up/gate，计算 SwiGLU，可生成 FP4 scale。但当前 RTX 6000D `sm120` 编译失败，报 `expects arch to be one of [Arch.sm_100a, Arch.sm_103a], got Arch.sm_120a`。
457	- TensorRT-LLM/FlashInfer SM120 TMA grouped MoE 代码明确限制：`TMA Warp Specialized Grouped GEMM specialisation doesn't support fused activation`。这解释了 dense-as-MoE 只有约 1% 收益。
458	
459	SM120 blockscale epilogue 探针：
460	
461	脚本：`bench/kernels/minicpm/bench_fp4_blockscale_epilogue_sm120.py`。
462	
463	结果（RTX 6000D，`M=1024,K=4096,N=4096` synthetic）：
464	
465	| 路径 | time |
466	|---|---:|
467	| baseline FP4 GEMM -> BF16 | 0.0935ms |
468	| BF16 post FP4 quant | 0.0203ms |
469	| direct FP4 blockscale epilogue | 0.0620ms |
470	
471	`out_fp4` / `out_sf` 可直接喂现有 `fp4_gemm` down path（`y_sf.view(m, n//16)`）。对比“BF16 落地后再量化”的 down-stream 输出：`max_diff=0.0072, mean_diff=0.000895, ref_abs_mean=0.0260`。这不是 bitwise 等价，但属于可接受的 FP4 量化舍入差异；后续以 e2e 精度/线上验证为准，不再把 bitwise 作为 fused epilogue 的硬目标。
472	
473	e2e 边界：当前 MiniCPM 在线主路径没有“FP4 GEMM 输出 BF16 后立刻 FP4 quant，且中间无非线性”的合法替换点。MLP 是 `gate_up -> SwiGLU -> quant -> down`，direct blockscale epilogue 只能证明“GEMM 直接输出 FP4”底座有收益，不能直接替换 MLP gate_up。真实 e2e 收益必须来自下一步 gated epilogue（accumulator 内直接 `silu(gate)*up` 后输出 FP4）。
474	
475	已否决的中间路线：
476	
477	脚本：`bench/kernels/minicpm/bench_mlp_fp4_intermediate_swiglu.py`（临时脚本已删除，仅保留结论）。
478	
479	尝试把 `gate_up GEMM` 先直接输出 FP4 gate/up，再用 CUDA kernel 做 `dequant gate/up -> SwiGLU -> FP4 quant`，最后接现有 down GEMM。这个路线避免 BF16 gate_up 中间态，但会在非线性前提前 FP4 量化。
480	
481	结果（`M=1024,H=4096,I=4096` synthetic）：
482	
483	| 路径 | time |
484	|---|---:|
485	| baseline gate_up BF16 GEMM | 0.1287ms |
486	| baseline sgl BF16 SwiGLU+FP4 quant | 0.0224ms |
487	| direct gate_up FP4 GEMM | 0.1057ms |
488	| FP4 gate/up SwiGLU+requant kernel | 0.1218ms |
489	
490	路径合计 `0.1511ms -> 0.2274ms`，更慢；down-stream 数值也明显恶化：`mean_diff=1.852 > ref_abs_mean=1.369`，而当前 sgl fused quant 对 BF16 reference 的 `mean_diff=0.0299`。结论：**不能先把 gate/up 中间态压成 FP4 再做 SwiGLU**。性能和精度都不成立。
491	
492	下一步高 ROI 路径：
493	
494	1. 做 SM120 dense-only `gate_up_swiglu_fp4` kernel，而不是继续套 MoE runner。
495	2. 复用 FlashInfer SM120 FP4 GEMM mainloop/tactic，新增 gated blockscale epilogue：
496	   - 输入权重需要从 MiniCPM `[gate, up]` 转为 epilogue友好的 `[up32, gate32, ...]` 或 `[up64, gate64, ...]`。
497	   - epilogue 取成对 accumulator，计算 `silu(gate) * up`。
498	   - 输出 layout 必须直接兼容 `down_proj.forward_fp4_quantized` 需要的 `x_fp4` 和 swizzled/block scale。
499	3. 精度要求：不追求 bitwise；先测 down-stream 数值差异，再做真实请求 / 公开集验证。若 e2e 精度可接受，优先保留 FP32 accumulator direct quantization，因为它才是性能最优路径。
500	
501	## 4. 后续工作流
502	
503	每个新优化必须留下：
504	
505	1. profile 证据（哪里热）。
506	2. 离线一致性（启用 shape + 边界 shape）。
507	3. 在线 debug 一致性（真实请求路径打印命中）。

510	6. profile 复核：热点确实下降，没转成新热点。
511	7. 文档 + commit：可复现命令、关键结果、风险边界。

```
101	    samples = []
102	    for task, idx_list in DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RANGES.items():
103	        pool = sorted(by_task[task], key=lambda x: x["index"])
104	        for idx in idx_list[: args.per_task]:
105	            sample = next(x for x in pool if x["index"] == idx)

118	        except Exception as e:

123	        per_task_scores[task] = per_task_scores.get(task, 0.0) + score
124	        per_task_count[task] = per_task_count.get(task, 0) + 1
125	        results.append({

127	            "index": s["index"],
128	            "gold": s["gold"],

130	            "completion_tokens": r["completion_tokens"],

133	            "pred_tail": r["content"][-400:],
134	        })
135	        print(
136	            f"  [{i+1}/{len(samples)}] {task} idx={s['index']:>3} "
137	            f"pt={r['prompt_tokens']:>6} ct={r['completion_tokens']:>5} "
138	            f"wall={r['wall_s']:>6.1f}s score={score:.2f}"
139	        )
140	    total_wall = time.time() - t0
141	    summary = {

145	        },

147	        "n_samples": len(samples),
148	    }
```

tool_result WebFetch
```
# DuoAttention: Key Technical Questions Answered

## Models Tested
The paper evaluates several Transformer-based LLMs: "Llama-2-7B-chat," "Llama-2-7B-32K-Instruct," "Llama-3-[8,70]B-Instruct," and "Mistral-7B-v0.2-Instruct." All tested architectures use standard multi-head or grouped-query attention.

## Hybrid/Alternative Architectures
The paper does not address whether DuoAttention works with Mamba, GLA, or SSM+attention hybrid models. The method is specifically designed for Transformer architectures with attention mechanisms.

## Retrieval Head Identification Process
DuoAttention uses an **optimization-based approach without labeled data**. The method assigns trainable gate values to each attention head and optimizes them on a synthetic passkey-retrieval dataset. As stated, "the total number of trainable parameters is only thousands of floating-point numbers," requiring "only 2,000 steps" and completing "within several hours on an 8 GPU node."

## NIAH Performance
Yes, NIAH is preserved. The paper demonstrates that "DuoAttention retains all KV caches in the retrieval heads while discarding only those in the streaming heads," successfully handling "lengths up to 1048K tokens effectively" on needle-in-haystack tests.

## GQA Prefill Speedup
For GQA models, DuoAttention achieves "up to 1.63× latency reduction" during prefilling with optimal configurations.

## Fine-tuning Requirements
DuoAttention requires **no model fine-tuning or retraining**. Only gate values are optimized while "all other model parameters remain frozen," preserving the original model's capabilities.
```

```
Web search results for query: ""Some attention is all you need" arXiv 2510 hybrid retrieval head ablation NIAH"

Links: [{"title":"Some Attention is All You Need for Retrieval","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2510.19861"},{"title":"[2510.19861] Some Attention is All You Need for Retrieval","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19861"},{"title":"Some Attention is All You Need for Retrieval Felix Michalak∗","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.19861"}]

I found the paper! Here's what the search results show:

The paper demonstrates complete functional segregation in hybrid SSM-Transformer architectures, where retrieval depends exclusively on self-attention layers.

**Key findings:**

- Across RecurrentGemma-2B/9B and Jamba-Mini-1.6, attention ablation causes catastrophic retrieval failure (0% accuracy), while SSM layers show no compensatory mechanisms even with improved prompting.

- Sparsifying attention to just 15% of heads maintains near-perfect retrieval while preserving 84% MMLU performance, suggesting self-attention specializes primarily for retrieval tasks.

- The paper identifies precise mechanistic requirements for retrieval: needle tokens must be exposed during generation and sufficient context must be available during prefill or generation.

**Methodology:**

The researchers employ entropy-based attention sparsification to progressively ablate attention mechanisms while monitoring retrieval performance on the Needle-In-A-Haystack (NIAH) benchmark. They complement this with Just Read Twice (JRT) prompting to attempt recovery of SSM-based retrieval capabilities.

The paper is arxiv 2510.19861 and was published on October 21, 2025.
```

```
Based on the search results, I found comprehensive information about InfLLM-V2 and its integration with OpenBMB's MiniCPM models. Here are the key findings:

## InfLLM-V2 Overview

InfLLM-V2 is a dense-sparse switchable attention framework that is a trainable sparse attention seamlessly adapting models from short to long sequences. It reuses dense attention parameters through parameter-free architecture modification, maintaining consistency between short and long sequence processing.

## Performance and Efficiency

InfLLM-V2 is 4× faster than dense attention while retaining 98.1% and 99.7% of the performance on long-context understanding and chain-of-thought reasoning, respectively. It ensures computational efficiency across all sequence lengths, by using dense attention for short inputs and smoothly transitioning to sparse attention for long sequences.

## Prefill and Decoding Acceleration

InfLLM v2 is a trainable sparse attention capable of prefilling and decoding acceleration, featuring efficient kernel design and end-to-end specialized training. It proposes an efficient Top-K context block selection method, which can reduce 60% computational costs compared with NSA.

## MiniCPM Integration

Based on the InfLLM-V2 framework, OpenBMB has trained and open-sourced MiniCPM4.1, a hybrid reasoning model providing a reproducible implementation for the research community. Additionally, MiniCPM-SALA innovatively integrates 25% sparse attention (InfLLM-V2) with 75% linear attention (Lightning Attention) for million-token context modeling.

## Paper Details

The InfLLM-V2 paper was released on September 29, 2025, and is available on arXiv as paper 2509.24663.
```

5	| 维度 | 决策 |
6	|---|---|
7	| Triangle layer 集合 | **由 gradient probe 决定**（P1 输出），不预设拍脑袋数字 |
8	| 跟 InfLLM-v2 共存 | 同一 server 内 layer-level dispatch：probe 选出的低 contribution 层走 Triangle，其余 std layer 保留 InfLLM-v2 sparse（ctx≥16K）/ dense FA（ctx<16K） |
9	| 跟 EAGLE-3 spec 共存 | **永远启用 Triangle**（不区分 NO_SPEC vs spec batch）。EAGLE aux layer 22 也可被选为 Triangle。target verify path 不动 |
10	| Draft model | 可重训（CLAUDE.md 中"不动 draft baseline"放开）。本期不重训，accept rate 退化可接受 |
11	| chunked prefill 末段 dense | 区分 last/non-last chunk：`is_last_chunk = (extend_prefix_lens + extend_seq_lens == seq_lens)`。仅 last chunk 切 q 末 n_last 段 dense |
12	| 短 ctx | `max(seq_lens) < SGLANG_TRIANGLEMIX_MIN_CTX=16384` 时 bypass，走原 dense FA |
13	
14	## Phase 序列
15	
16	phase 间是 dependency 关系，每 phase 完成判据是**正确性测试**（不是 ROI 决策）。每 phase 都依赖前面的产物，按顺序推进。
17	
18	### P1 — Gradient probe calibration
19	
20	**目标**：用本仓 base BF16 model + 长 ctx 样本，算 8 个 std layer (id [0,9,16,17,22,29,30,31]) 的 middle-Q-K contribution，按 contribution 排序，选出 Triangle layer 集合。
21	
22	**做什么**
23	- `bench/trianglemix/probe_layer_contribution.py`：HF transformers 加载 BF16 base model（量化前的，平台 `--input` 给的版本；本机如无，先用 NVFP4 dequant 近似 BF16）
24	- Hook 8 个 std FA layer 的 softmax 输出，乘 element-wise probe variable θ_{l,i,j}
25	- 用 perf_public_set 的 5-10 个长样本（cwe + niah 各几个），forward + backward
26	- 在 middle-Q-K 区域（sink + window + last 之外）累加 `|∂y_gt/∂θ|`
27	- 输出每 std layer 的归一化 contribution 值
28	
29	**完成判据**

```
1	"""Sparse metadata kernels for MiniCPM long-context attention."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import torch
6	import triton
7	import triton.language as tl
8	
9	
10	@triton.jit
11	def _topk_to_flashinfer_indices_kernel(
12	    topk_ptr,
13	    base_page_table_ptr,
14	    token_to_bs_ptr,
15	    token_pos_ptr,
16	    seqlen_k_ptr,
17	    kv_indptr_ptr,
18	    kv_indices_ptr,
19	    kv_last_page_len_ptr,
20	    topk_stride_h: tl.constexpr,
21	    topk_stride_token: tl.constexpr,
22	    topk_stride_k: tl.constexpr,
23	    base_pt_stride_bs: tl.constexpr,
24	    base_pt_stride_pos: tl.constexpr,
25	    sparse_topk: tl.constexpr,
26	    block_size: tl.constexpr,
27	    head_groups: tl.constexpr,
28	):
29	    row = tl.program_id(0)
30	    token = row // head_groups
31	    head_group = row - token * head_groups
32	    block_offsets = tl.arange(0, block_size)
33	
34	    bs = tl.load(token_to_bs_ptr + token).to(tl.int64)
35	    token_pos = tl.load(token_pos_ptr + token)
36	    seqlen_k = tl.load(seqlen_k_ptr + bs)
37	    limit = tl.minimum(token_pos, seqlen_k)
38	    dst_base = tl.load(kv_indptr_ptr + row).to(tl.int64)
39	    row_n = tl.full((), 0, tl.int32)
40	
41	    for topk_i in range(0, sparse_topk):
42	        block = tl.load(
43	            topk_ptr
44	            + head_group * topk_stride_h
45	            + token * topk_stride_token
46	            + topk_i * topk_stride_k
47	        )
48	        pos = block * block_size + block_offsets
49	        mask_t = (block >= 0) & (pos < limit)
50	        base_page = tl.load(
51	            base_page_table_ptr
52	            + bs * base_pt_stride_bs
53	            + pos * base_pt_stride_pos,
54	            mask=mask_t,
55	            other=0,
56	        ).to(tl.int64)
57	        pages = (base_page * head_groups + head_group).to(tl.int32)
58	        tl.store(kv_indices_ptr + dst_base + row_n + block_offsets, pages, mask=mask_t)
59	        row_n += tl.sum(mask_t.to(tl.int32), axis=0)
60
```

```
# InfLLM-V2 Overview

**What it is:**
InfLLM-V2 is a "trainable sparse attention" framework that enables language models to process long sequences efficiently. It uses a dense-sparse switchable design—employing dense attention for short inputs and transitioning to sparse attention for longer sequences.

**Training requirements:**
The paper indicates InfLLM-V2 "seamlessly adapts models from short to long sequences" and uses a "parameter-free architecture modification," suggesting it requires fine-tuning rather than being training-free. The authors explicitly note it overcomes limitations by maintaining the "pretrain-on-short, finetune-on-long" workflow.

**Performance metrics available:**
The abstract reports that InfLLM-V2 achieves "4× faster than dense attention while retaining 98.1% and 99.7% of the performance" on long-context understanding and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks, respectively.

**Information gaps:**
The webpage content does not provide specific details about:
- NIAH (Needle in a Haystack) performance
- Prefill speedup metrics
- Hybrid architecture performance with few attention layers
- MiniCPM-SALA-specific implementation details

These specifics would likely appear in the full paper PDF rather than the abstract provided here.
```

```
Based on the search results, I found several relevant papers on distributed and efficient attention mechanisms for long-context LLM inference. Here are the key findings:

## Star Attention

Star Attention is a two-phase block-sparse approximation that improves computational efficiency by sharding attention across multiple hosts while minimizing communication overhead. When the block size remains fixed and the sequence length increases, Star Attention achieves exponential speedup over Ring Attention at the cost of slightly more accuracy degradation. Star Attention maintains 97-100% of the accuracy of global attention, and in some cases, even outperforms it.

## Related Attention Mechanisms

Several other efficient attention approaches for long-context inference are discussed:

- **Dynamic Sparse Attention**: MInference is a sparse calculation method designed to accelerate pre-filling of long-sequence processing by identifying three unique patterns in long-context attention matrices—the A-shape, Vertical-Slash, and Block-Sparse.

- **Distributed Prefilling**: Sequence parallelism partitions the sequence across devices (termed as hosts) and significantly improves the prefill speed, especially for extremely long inputs.

- **Hybrid Models**: SSM and hybrid models are being adopted in the industry due to strong scaling over context length, with examples including Falcon-H1 series using a parallel hybrid architecture combining Transformer attention with Mamba-2 SSMs.

The arXiv paper on Star Attention is identified as arXiv:2411.17116 and represents recent work in 2024 on distributed long-context inference techniques.
```

```
## Key Findings:

**Hybrid Model Architectures:**
There is a surge in interest in hybrid architectures that interleave attention and RNN layers, achieving a favorable tradeoff between model performance and inference throughput. Hybrid Transformer architectures, which combine softmax attention blocks and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), have shown a desirable performance-throughput tradeoff for long-context modeling.

**Efficient Attention Mechanisms:**
Linear attention methods achieve linear complexity through kernel approximations, recurrent formulations, or fast-weight dynamics, thereby enabling scalable inference with reduced computational overhead. Additionally, sparse attention techniques limit attention computation to selected subsets of tokens based on fixed patterns, block-wise routing, or clustering strategies, enhancing efficiency while preserving contextual coverage.

**Training-Free Sparse Attention:**
The search results mention training-free and post-training techniques for sparse attention, with recent research introducing natively trainable sparse attention mechanisms, among which native sparse attention stands out as the most widely recognized and promising approach.

**Linear Attention Methods (GLA and Related):**
Modern RNN mixers compatible with hybrid architectures include Lightning attention, Mamba2, GLA, GDN, and RWKV-7. FLA provides a variety of subquadratic kernels/layers/models including RetNet/GLA/Mamba/HGRN/HGRN2/RWKV6.

**Prefill Acceleration:**
The chunkwise representation is typically adopted during the training and prefill stages, and recent models like MiniCPM-SALA employs a hybrid architecture of sparse and linear attention specifically designed to achieve efficient ultra-long sequence modeling.
```

# LeanK: Learnable K Cache Channel Pruning for Efficient Decoding

Building upon the observation that QK vectors are **statically sparse** in the **channel (head_dim)** dimension, LeanK uses a learning-based approach to obtain channel-wise static mask used for KV Cache pruning.

Experiments demonstrate up to **70%** K cache and **16%–18%** V cache memory reduction, reduces GPU memory and accelerates decoding without sacrificing accuracy.

<p align="center">
  <img src="./assets/leank_method.png"=width="700">
</p>


### Quick Start: Use LeanK with pretrained static channel patterns

Requirement: install the latest version of minference and tilelang

Add the following patch to enable LeanK decoding patched on Huggingface transformers:

```diff
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
+ from minference import MInference

model_name = "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_name,
    torch_dtype="auto",
    device_map="cuda",
    _attn_implementation="flash_attention_2",
)

+minference_patch = MInference(
+    attn_type="dense", model_name=model_name, kv_type="leank"
+)
+model = minference_patch(model)

prompt = open("narrativeqa_example.txt").read()
batch_inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")

outputs = model.generate(**batch_inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
generated_text = tokenizer.decode(
    outputs[0][batch_inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=True
)
print(f"Generated text: {generated_text!r}")
```

Note: for unseen sequence length, Tilelang kernel compilation may take considerable longer time. It will be much faster once the kernel is compiled and kept in cache.

```
# MiniCPM-SALA: Hybrid Attention for Long Contexts

## Overview
MiniCPM-SALA is a 9B-parameter model combining sparse and linear attention mechanisms to efficiently handle ultra-long contexts (up to 1M tokens). Rather than using 8 standard + 24 specialized layers, it employs a "1:3 ratio" architecture: 25% sparse attention (InfLLM-V2) and 75% linear attention (Lightning Attention).

## Architecture Details
The paper states the model uses "a layer selection algorithm to integrate these mechanisms in a 1:3 ratio," rather than uniform interleaving. This algorithmic placement outperforms naive distribution approaches. All layers retain Feed-Forward Network blocks for knowledge capacity.

## Prefill Challenges
The paper addresses prefilling through substantial inference speed improvements. At 256K tokens on an A6000D GPU, MiniCPM-SALA achieves 51.6 seconds Time To First Token versus Qwen3's 180.8 seconds—representing "3.5× the inference speed" gains.

## Sparse Attention Acceleration
The paper does not discuss further acceleration of InfLLM-V2 sparse layers. It notes InfLLM-V2's "distinct advantage of introducing no additional parameters," but focuses on demonstrating the hybrid approach's effectiveness rather than optimizing individual components.

## Ablation Studies
The document contains no ablations on reducing attention layers or increasing sparsity. The fixed 1:3 ratio appears as a design choice based on prior research rather than empirically validated through systematic ablations.
```

```
Based on the search results, here's what I found about these topics from 2025 research:

## DuoAttention

DuoAttention is a framework that only applies a full KV cache to retrieval heads while using a light-weight, constant-length KV cache for streaming heads, which reduces both LLM's decoding and pre-filling memory and latency without compromising its long-context abilities. DuoAttention provides comparable accuracy as full attention on the Needle-in-a-Haystack benchmark using 25% full attention ratio on the MHA model and 50% full attention ratio on the GQA model. DuoAttention achieves up to 2.45× memory reduction for MHA and 1.65× for GQA models, along with up to 2.13× latency reduction for MHA and 1.5× for GQA models.

## Hybrid Mamba-GLA and Linear Attention Approaches

MiniCPM-SALA is a 9B-parameter hybrid architecture that integrates the high-fidelity long-context modeling of sparse attention (InfLLM-V2) with the global efficiency of linear attention (Lightning Attention). Later architectures keep the same overall idea but swap in other lightweight sequence mixers, such as Kimi Delta Attention, Lightning Attention, or standard Mamba-2.

## Mamba-Transformer Hybrids

A 1:1 SSM-to-attention ratio is typical in hybrid models, though some prefer more SSM layers for efficiency. Previous works often finetune models on synthetic tasks like Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH), which boosts recall but often harms performance on other metrics. To mitigate this, continued training with paraphrased sentences from a distribution similar to the pretraining data enhances recall with minimum or no degradation in commonsense reasoning.
```

```
Based on the search results, here's what I found about FlexPrefill:

## Overview

FlexPrefill is a Flexible sparse Pre-filling mechanism that dynamically adjusts sparse attention patterns and computational budget in real-time to meet the specific requirements of each input and attention head.

## The Problem It Addresses

Large language models (LLMs) encounter computational challenges during long-sequence inference, especially in the attention pre-filling phase, where the complexity grows quadratically with the prompt length. Previous efforts to mitigate these challenges have relied on fixed sparse attention patterns or identifying sparse attention patterns based on limited cases, but these methods lacked the flexibility to efficiently adapt to varying input demands.

## Key Innovations

FlexPrefill features two main innovations:

1. Query-Aware Sparse Pattern Determination: By measuring Jensen-Shannon divergence, this component adaptively switches between query-specific diverse attention patterns and predefined attention patterns.

2. Cumulative-Attention Based Index Selection: This component dynamically selects query-key indexes to be computed based on different attention patterns, ensuring the sum of attention scores meets a predefined threshold.

## Results and Recognition

Experimental results show significant improvements in both speed and accuracy over prior methods, providing a more flexible and efficient solution for LLM inference. Additionally, FlexPrefill is selected as Oral Presentation (1.77%) at ICLR 2025!

The paper (arXiv:2502.20766) was posted on February 28, 2025.
```

```
Based on the search results, I found relevant research on hybrid models combining attention and state space models (SSMs), with discussions of bottlenecks and computational challenges. Here are the key findings:

## Hybrid Models and Computational Bottlenecks

Hymba faces computational efficiency challenges where the two branches process inputs at different speeds, causing the faster branch to idle while waiting for the slower one, ultimately leading to TPS bottlenecks. This directly addresses the "cannot accelerate" theme in your query.

The faster branch must still idle until its slower counterpart completes its computation before the fused representation can be passed onward, causing a synchronization bottleneck that limits the computational efficiency of the model.

## Retrieval and Attention Challenges in SSMs

Research on SSMs and hybrid architectures has revealed fundamental limitations in retrieval tasks. SSMs underperform on tasks requiring non-standard retrieval, and proposed hybrid architectures to address this limitation. More specifically, while these limitations exist, they originate from a small subset of heads responsible for retrieval rather than the entire language model.

## Gated Linear Attention (GLA)

GLA directly introduces gating mechanism in the Linear Attention, where a gating function is embedded into a linearized attention layer to improve its expressiveness.

## Throughput Trade-offs

Attention-based models occupy a different region of the tradeoff frontier than SSMs, with stronger recall but higher computational cost.

These findings suggest that recent work in 2024-2025 is exploring the tension between computational efficiency and model performance in hybrid attention-SSM architectures, with particular attention to retrieval bottlenecks.
```

```
## MInference 1.0: Overview

MInference (Milliontokens Inference) is a sparse calculation method designed to accelerate pre-filling of long-sequence processing. It identifies three unique patterns in long-context attention matrices—the A-shape, Vertical-Slash, and Block-Sparse—that can be leveraged for efficient sparse computation on GPUs.

## Performance and Hybrid Approach

The method determines the optimal pattern for each attention head offline and dynamically builds sparse indices based on the assigned pattern during inference. With the pattern and sparse indices, it performs efficient sparse attention calculations via optimized GPU kernels to significantly reduce the latency in the pre-filling stage of long-context LLMs. MInference effectively reduces inference latency by up to 10x for pre-filling on an A100, while maintaining accuracy.

## Recent Extensions

A multi-modality work called MMInference uses modality-aware permutation sparse attention to accelerate long-context VLMs (Vision Language Models). MMInference has been accepted at ICML'25.

I did not find specific information about an "MInference 2.0" or "v2" release in the search results. The most recent development appears to be MMInference, which extends the approach to multi-modal models rather than a newer version of MInference itself.
```

```
# Summary of Paper: Understanding and Enhancing Mamba-Transformer Hybrids

## Paper Focus
This research analyzes hybrid models combining state-space models (Mamba) with attention mechanisms, examining how architectural design affects performance on memory recall and language modeling tasks.

## Sparsity of Feed-Forward Layers
The paper does **not** discuss making feed-forward (FF) layers sparse. Instead, it examines FF layer placement, finding that adding FF layers to only one component degrades performance; they must be added to both components for improvements.

## Key Findings About Attention in Hybrids

The research identifies several important insights:

- **Sequential vs. Parallel Integration**: "Sequential models excel in short contexts, parallel models excel in long ones," with sequential hybrids showing higher output embedding similarity between components.

- **Merge-Attention Aggregation**: Parallel models using merge-attention (an attention layer fusing SSM and attention outputs) achieve superior performance, particularly for long-context recall.

- **Representational Diversity**: Parallel architectures maintain "much lower similarity" between component outputs, preserving distinct representational strengths.

## Training Approach
This is **not** training-free. The paper employs two strategies: architectural experiments during pretraining on 100B tokens, plus continual training on paraphrased datasets for recall enhancement.

## NIAH Results
The paper mentions NIAH (Needle-in-a-Haystack) as a baseline dataset but notes it "significantly harm[s] commonsense performance," unlike their paraphrased approach, which achieves better performance trade-offs.
```

```
I found information about SeerAttention from arXiv 2410. Here are the key results:

## SeerAttention Overview

SeerAttention is a simple yet effective attention mechanism that directly learns the block-level attention sparsity from the LLM itself. Inspired by the gating mechanism in Mixture of Experts (MoE), SeerAttention augments the conventional attention with a learnable gate that selectively activates important blocks within the attention map.

## Technical Approach

The gate first pools the query (Q) and key (K) tensors along the sequence dimension and processes them through learnable linear layers. The resulting matrices are then multiplied together to produce the gating scores, which are used to predict block-level attention sparsity.

## Performance Results

When applied to long-context fine-tuning with YaRN, SeerAttention can achieve a remarkable 90% sparsity ratio at a 32k context length with minimal perplexity loss, offering a 5.67x speedup over FlashAttention-2. SeerAttention achieves better model accuracy and lower latency for long-context pre-filling compared to prior methods.

## Training Approach

When applied to pre-trained LLMs, SeerAttention only requires training the gate parameters in a lightweight self-distillation manner, allowing rapid convergence.

The paper was published in October 2024 (arXiv:2410.13276) and provides a learnable sparse attention solution that contrasts with earlier predefined pattern-based sparse attention methods.
```
